draft.title: Australia's free trade agreements
card: A free trade agreement (FTA) is a deal between countries to cut or remove tariffs and other trade barriers on the goods and services they trade with each other.
an FTA between two countries. Australia has these with partners such as China, Japan, Korea and the United States.
an FTA among several countries in a region. Australia is part of RCEP and the CPTPP, which link it with many Asia-Pacific economies at once.
An FTA lowers barriers only for its members. Trade with countries outside the deal can still face the usual tariffs.
draft.remember: An FTA cuts trade barriers among its members. Australia has both two-country and regional deals.

a.q: Which describes Australia's agreement with Japan?
opts: A bilateral FTA cutting barriers between two countries
A regional FTA linking many Asia-Pacific economies
A tariff Australia applies to all of its trading partners
A deal cutting barriers for every country Australia trades with
a.why: Japan is one partner, so the deal is bilateral, and it cuts barriers between the two members. A regional FTA such as RCEP or the CPTPP involves several countries at once.
a.clue: Count how many countries are in the deal.

b.q: Australia joins an FTA with a group of Asia-Pacific countries and its tariffs on their goods fall. What is the likely effect on trade with a non-member country?
opts: Its goods still face the usual tariffs into Australia
Its goods get the same lower tariffs as the members
Its goods are banned from entering Australia
Its goods become cheaper than goods from the members
b.why: An FTA lowers barriers only for its members, so a non-member still faces the usual tariffs. The lower tariffs do not extend to every trading partner.
b.clue: Who gets the lower barriers under an FTA?
